_comment: Forts as strongholds (field.json fort is where and how one is first built). A fort has its own buildings on plots: the Keep (`keep`), the Storage (`storage`) and three wall rings round them, inner to outer (`rings`, plots w0-w2), each with its wall building and its slots for towers (plots t<ring>-<slot>). A fort starts with the Keep and the Storage at level 1. Its buildings rise one at a time (each level's cost is `cost` x `costGrowth`^(level-1), paid from the village that built it; done after `buildSeconds` x `timeGrowth`^(level-1) real seconds, divided by world speed). A ring's wall can be built once the Keep reaches its `keepLevel`, costs its `costFactor` of the village wall (buildings.json wall), as do the towers on it (the village's tower kinds), and rises to `wallMaxLevel`; its towers open once its wall stands and never rise above it. The Keep's zone of influence reaches `zone.base` hexes, one more every `zone.every` Keep levels after the first: the village that built the fort can reshape the land and build roads within it as near its own walls. The Storage keeps `storage.grainBase` + `storage.grainPerLevel` per level of grain. The Fort Garrison (`garrison`, plot `garrison`) keeps `garrison.perLevel` defenders for each of its levels: they never leave the fort, fight in its battles in `garrison.stance`, and, while the fort has grain, one fallen defender comes back every `garrison.musterHours` game hours, free (the kind most short first). Upkeep: a standing fort eats `upkeep.grainPerHour` grain a game hour, `upkeep.perKeepLevel` more for each Keep level and `upkeep.perDefender` for each defender, counted every `upkeep.everyHours` game hours; when its grain runs out its defenders desert. A fort with defenders counts as held: hordes keep out of its zone of control, and one that marches on it fights them. Sieges: a horde battering a fort meets its wall rings from the outside in; each built ring stands with the integrity, defense, archers and towers of a village's walls of its level (walls.json), and once battered down the next takes its place; each ring breached loses walls.json breachLevelsLost levels when the battle ends. While a ring stands nobody maneuvers. A fort with no grain and no army holding it for `takeoverHours` game hours is taken by bandits: a camp of `banditUnits` units. A fort or supply point can be torn down; whatever it stored is lost.

keep.name: Keep
keep.description: The fort's heart. Each level widens the land the fort's village can reshape and build roads on; levels 4 and 7 open the middle and the outer wall.

garrison.name: Fort Garrison
garrison.description: Quarters for the fort's own defenders: a few spearmen, archers and horsemen for every level, who never leave the fort. The fallen are replaced, one at a time.

storage.name: Storage
storage.description: The fort's grain store: for the armies holding it and for its own upkeep.
